newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares extend gains on privatisation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares extend gains on privatisation hopes.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended weekly gains on Wednesday amid privatisation hopes which remained high ahead of Thursday's meeting of the Higher Board of Privatisation, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed 29 points, or 1.8 percent higher at 1,636, bringing gains to 9.1 percent so far this week after last week's 3.88 percent rise caused by fading political tension.
The index brushed a high of 1,642 in the afternoon before easing on profit-taking.
Trade volume dropped to 41.5 trillion lira from Tuesday's 44.69 trillion.
Privatisation hopes which enlivened on Monday due to the meeting of the Higher Board scheduled for Thursday has fuelled buying in state firms this week.

The Board, gathering for the first time since mid-January is expected to approve 19 sell off tenders whose negotiations were finalised in December and January. Total value of the best bids in these tenders were $881.7 million.
"The market expects concrete results from the meeting which will mean that new sell off revenues will be registered as income for the Treasury," said Ilker Akar from Taib investment.
"Tomorrow will also be an important day for bluechip Eregli because the Board will decide whether to consider the two bids received in its tender," he said.
Only two bids from local groups were received in a January tender for the block sale of a 30-40 percent state share in flat steel maker Eregli.

The most heavily traded shares were those of Turkish Airlines which rose 5,000 lira to 43,000 as the company declared soaring 1996 net profits. It was followed by other largely state owned firms -- Eregli, up 1,000 lira at 18,750 and oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 77,000. They made up 25.2 percent of the total turnover.
"The index may test (its all-time high close of 1,700) if decisions reached at tomorrow's meeting are likely to be carried out," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.
"Political winds have died down and there is no significant movement in alternative markets. So the stock market is moving with its own dynamics," he added.
Of the 239 shares traded, 120 advanced, 69 declined and 50 were stable.
